newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end lower on fears of higher rates.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end lower on fears of higher rates.

text.p: April 11 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.05 99.09
Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures settled lower on Friday, dampened by a series of fresh official comments suggesting higher Japanese interest rates.
Talk of higher interest rates spread after comments late on Thursday by senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara suggesting that the yen bond market had overshot.
The December was 99.05 after moving in 99.04-99.08 range.
Turnover was 49,919 contracts.
Such talk was further fuelled by a limited impact on the foreign exchange market from Thursday's verbal "interventions" by Japanese and U.S. officials, traders said.
"There was a view spread overseas that the sole way to stop the yen's fall would be a rise in Japanese interest rates," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank.
Early on Friday, cabinet minister Kabun Muto said Japan should increase its official discount rate by the end of this year to discourage capital outflows from Japan.
This comment, however, failed to trigger aggressive sales.

Traders said a majority in Tokyo still believe the Bank of Japan (BOJ) is unlikely to change its low interest rate policy in the April-June period as the bank has said it will watch the impact on the economy of a tax increase from April 1.
"To keep the yen from falling, MOF wants a steepening in the yield curve. But the BOJ is not ready to raise short-term interest rates for now," said another long-term bank dealer.

A trust bank dealer said the December contract seemed vulnerable to falls towards 98.95 because Euroyen cash rates failed to ease even after banks' seasonal fund demand before and after the fiscal year-end had finished.
Some said recent upward pressure in the short end of the yield curve was attributed to a remaining imbalance in fund supply and demand, which had started before March 31.

"Given the BOJ's low interest rate policy, banks focused ahead of the fiscal year-end on raising overnight money, while end-investors looked for higher-yield bonds. Even though the fiscal year-end factor is over, both sides seem happy to maintain such attitudes," a market analyst said.
The BOJ may have to maintain its accommodative credit stance when the next bank reserves period starts next week in order to keep the key overnight call rate from rising, he said.
The key overnight call rate usually drops when a new one-month bank reserve period starts because banks are no longer in a hurry to raise funds for deposits at the BOJ.
The BOJ maintained its accommodative credit stance this morning. The BOJ left the money market in surplus by about 100 billion yen on Friday, unchanged from Thursday.
Given the operation as expected, the key overnight call rate eased to 0.49 percent from Thursday's 0.51 percent.
About 120 billion yen worth of benchmark three-month certificates of deposit were issued at an unchanged 0.55 percent. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
